findings.title: Ownership verification silently falls back for unobserved paths and omits trusted Nix database
findings.observation: verify_requisites uses verify_nonwritable when bind_path_for_ownership returns None. That branch accepts an unobserved root/overflow-owned selected file without pinned host inode/device evidence. Actual /usr/bin/env takes that branch; tests explicitly endorse it. os.access follows symlink target while owner check uses lstat(link), so target host-root ownership is not established there. The pinned query binary is likewise outside the K requisites and lacks a bound root entry; /nix/var/nix/db and db.sqlite are not referenced or checked. Actual inspected DB is currently UID0 and nonwritable, but the required preflight predicate is absent.
findings.impact: Arbitrary overflow owner is accepted for selected paths despite adopted prohibition, and the database relied on for registered NAR trust is not included in runtime protected-path validation.
findings.repair: Extend host evidence to selected links, resolved executable targets, query-tool package and trusted database/ancestor paths. Reject missing host binding rather than falling back to UID/nonwritability only. Validate mapping, correct stat identity and effective nonwritability for those concrete paths under strong containment.
